questions.q: How does a honeybee tell her sisters where to find flowers?
questions.fact: She dances! A forager bee does a 'waggle dance' on the honeycomb to show the other bees which way to fly and how far to go.

questions.q: What does the 'waggle' part of the dance show?
choices: The direction and distance to the food
questions.fact: Direction and distance! The angle of the waggle points the way compared to the sun, and a longer waggle means the flowers are farther away.

questions.q: What dance do bees do when the flowers are very close to the hive?
questions.fact: The round dance! When food is close by, a bee runs in little circles to say 'it's nearby, go look around!'

questions.q: Where do honeybees usually do their dances?
choices: On the honeycomb inside the dark hive
questions.fact: Inside the dark hive! The other bees can't see much in there, so they follow the dancer closely and feel her moves and vibrations.
